1: # Instructions
2: 
3: Compute the result for a game of Hex / Polygon.
4: 
5: The abstract boardgame known as [Hex][hex] / Polygon / CON-TAC-TIX is quite simple in rules, though complex in practice.
6: Two players place stones on a parallelogram with hexagonal fields.
7: The player to connect his/her stones to the opposite side first wins.
8: The four sides of the parallelogram are divided between the two players (i.e. one player gets assigned a side and the side directly opposite it and the other player gets assigned the two other sides).
9: 
10: Your goal is to build a program that given a simple representation of a board computes the winner (or lack thereof).
11: Note that all games need not be "fair".
12: (For example, players may have mismatched piece counts or the game's board might have a different width and height.)
13: 
14: The boards look like this:
15: 
16: ```text
17: . O . X .
18:  . X X O .
19:   O O O X .
20:    . X O X O
21:     X O O O X
22: ```
23: 
24: "Player `O`" plays from top to bottom, "Player `X`" plays from left to right.
25: In the above example `O` has made a connection from left to right but nobody has won since `O` didn't connect top and bottom.
26: 
27: [hex]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hex_%28board_game%29

```go
package connect

func ResultOf(board []string) (string, error) {
	rows := len(board)
	if rows == 0 {
		return "", nil
	}
	cols := len(board[0])

	if xWins(board, rows, cols) {
		return "X", nil
	}
	if oWins(board, rows, cols) {
		return "O", nil
	}
	return "", nil
}

// neighbors returns the six hex neighbors of cell (r, c).
func neighbors(r, c, rows, cols int) [][2]int {
	cands := [][2]int{
		{r - 1, c},
		{r - 1, c + 1},
		{r, c - 1},
		{r, c + 1},
		{r + 1, c - 1},
		{r + 1, c},
	}
	var out [][2]int
	for _, n := range cands {
		if n[0] >= 0 && n[0] < rows && n[1] >= 0 && n[1] < cols {
			out = append(out, n)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// connect checks whether the given player has a connected path from the
// starting edge to the opposite edge.
func connect(board []string, rows, cols int, player byte, vertical bool) bool {
	visited := make([][]bool, rows)
	for i := range visited {
		visited[i] = make([]bool, cols)
	}
	stack := [][2]int{}

	if vertical {
		// O: top to bottom
		for c := 0; c < cols; c++ {
			if board[0][c] == player {
				stack = append(stack, [2]int{0, c})
				visited[0][c] = true
			}
		}
	} else {
		// X: left to right
		for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
			if board[r][0] == player {
				stack = append(stack, [2]int{r, 0})
				visited[r][0] = true
			}
		}
	}

	for len(stack) > 0 {
		cell := stack[len(stack)-1]
		stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
		r, c := cell[0], cell[1]

		if vertical {
			if r == rows-1 {
				return true
			}
		} else {
			if c == cols-1 {
				return true
			}
		}

		for _, n := range neighbors(r, c, rows, cols) {
			nr, nc := n[0], n[1]
			if !visited[nr][nc] && board[nr][nc] == player {
				visited[nr][nc] = true
				stack = append(stack, [2]int{nr, nc})
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

func xWins(board []string, rows, cols int) bool {
	return connect(board, rows, cols, 'X', false)
}

func oWins(board []string, rows, cols int) bool {
	return connect(board, rows, cols, 'O', true)
}
```

```go
package connect

// ResultOf computes the winner of a game of Hex / Polygon.
//
// The board is a parallelogram of hexagonal fields. Each line is a row of the
// board; leading whitespace is only for readability and is ignored. Player "O"
// connects the top edge to the bottom edge, while player "X" connects the left
// edge to the right edge. The first player to complete such a connection wins.
func ResultOf(board []string) (string, error) {
	rows := len(board)
	if rows == 0 {
		return "", nil
	}
	cols := len(board[0])

	if connected(board, rows, cols, 'X', false) {
		return "X", nil
	}
	if connected(board, rows, cols, 'O', true) {
		return "O", nil
	}
	return "", nil
}

// connected reports whether player has a connected chain of stones running from
// one edge of the board to the opposite edge. When vertical is true the chain
// must run from the top edge to the bottom edge (player O); otherwise it must
// run from the left edge to the right edge (player X).
func connected(board []string, rows, cols int, player byte, vertical bool) bool {
	visited := make([][]bool, rows)
	for i := range visited {
		visited[i] = make([]bool, cols)
	}

	stack := make([][2]int, 0, rows*cols)
	if vertical {
		for c := 0; c < cols; c++ {
			if board[0][c] == player {
				visited[0][c] = true
				stack = append(stack, [2]int{0, c})
			}
		}
	} else {
		for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
			if board[r][0] == player {
				visited[r][0] = true
				stack = append(stack, [2]int{r, 0})
			}
		}
	}

	for len(stack) > 0 {
		r, c := stack[len(stack)-1]
		stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]

		if (vertical && r == rows-1) || (!vertical && c == cols-1) {
			return true
		}

		for _, n := range neighbors(r, c, rows, cols) {
			if !visited[n[0]][n[1]] && board[n[0]][n[1]] == player {
				visited[n[0]][n[1]] = true
				stack = append(stack, n)
			}
		}
	}

	return false
}

// neighbors returns the in-bounds hexagonal neighbours of cell (r, c). The board
// is a slanted parallelogram, so moving to the row above shifts the column by
// one and moving to the row below shifts it the other way.
func neighbors(r, c, rows, cols int) [][2]int {
	candidates := [][2]int{
		{r - 1, c},
		{r - 1, c + 1},
		{r, c - 1},
		{r, c + 1},
		{r + 1, c - 1},
		{r + 1, c},
	}
	neighbors := make([][2]int, 0, 6)
	for _, n := range candidates {
		if n[0] >= 0 && n[0] < rows && n[1] >= 0 && n[1] < cols {
			neighbors = append(neighbors, n)
		}
	}
	return neighbors
}
```

Implemented `ResultOf` in `connect.go` (the only file I touched — no new files, and `connect_test.go` is unchanged).

**Approach:** After the test harness strips whitespace, each board is a rectangular grid. I treat it as a slanted parallelogram and run a flood-fill (iterative DFS) for each player:

- **`neighbors`** — returns the six in-bounds hexagonal neighbors of a cell. Because the board slants, the row above contributes `(r-1, c)` and `(r-1, c+1)`, the row below contributes `(r+1, c-1)` and `(r+1, c)`, plus the horizontal `(r, c±1)`.
- **`connected`** — seeds the search from every stone of the given player on the starting edge, then checks whether the flood reaches the opposite edge.
- **`ResultOf`** — checks `X` for a left→right connection first, then `O` for a top→bottom connection, returning `"X"`, `"O"`, or `""`.
